Aisha (prod): Quick sync — we need to lock the long-term routing + isolation asks for the H2 roadmap. customer asks are piling up and sales needs concrete launch criteria.
Tom (infra): Agreed. High level proposal: 3 lanes — Hosted, Dedicated, Private. Each lane gets SLA/routing policies + eviction thresholds. Can we scope which policies are MVP vs v2?
Priya (arch): MVP should include region affinity, simple fallback (compatible model family), and tenant bandwidth caps. v2: per-tenant placement policies, soft-eviction, geo-residency windows.
Raj (eng): From implementation POV, region affinity + model-family fallback is doable in one sprint if we standardize policy DSL. Soft-eviction is heavier (stateful drains + metrics).
Lena (sales): Can you prioritize residency windows + an enterprise-grade Private onboarding checklist? A customer in EU will sign if we confirm data-residency SLAs and rollout gates.
Aisha (prod): Residency windows are high priority but need clarity: is the product going to promise hard stop (no egress) or best-effort placement? We need legal input for hard guarantees.
Priya (arch): Proposal: Promise placement (soft guarantee) with escape hatches: contractual SLA for Dedicated/Private, best-effort for Hosted. Document migration path if we can’t honor placement due to capacity.
Tom (infra): Operational constraints: we need capacity reservation primitives for Dedicated (reservations + burst pools). Otherwise routing will keep failing customers over time.
Raj (eng): Also need observability signals exposed to customers: per-request route decision, reason code (affinity, capacity, fallback), and measurable SLOs.
routing-bot: New RFC created: /rfc/trajectory-routing-206543 — includes policy DSL sketch and gating matrix. Link: https://redwood.internal/rfc/trajectory-routing-206543
Aisha (prod): Nice. Next: launch criteria. My suggestion: for initial GA (Hosted + Dedicated): (1) deterministic routing for 95% of traffic, (2) documented fallback behavior, (3) rollout playbook and customer-facing docs, (4) telemetry ingestion for routing reasons.
Priya (arch): Add: migration runbook for tenants moved due to capacity and an automated notification flow (email + console alert) for impacted tenants.
Lena (sales): And a commercial acceptance: Dedicated customers must have the ability to lock placement with a simple contract clause; Sales needs a templated language.
Tom (infra): Technical acceptance: end-to-end test harness that simulates multi-region saturation and validates fallbacks within latency SLOs. We should include perf benchmarks per model family.
Raj (eng): Dev tasks I see: policy DSL parser, route decision service (idempotent), capacity reservation API, KV for tenant placements, telemetry events. Estimate: 6 weeks for core pieces if we pull 2 engs + 1 infra.
Aisha (prod): Prioritization: Must-haves for GA: region affinity + fallback, capacity reservation API, customer-visible telemetry, rollout playbook. Nice-to-have: per-tenant placement UI, soft-eviction automation.
Priya (arch): Risks: cross-region bandwidth costs, complexity of pinned placements causing fragmentation, and failure modes when fallback model family isn't acceptable for customer (quality regressions).
Lena (sales): For the latter, we need an escalation path: escalate to a human ops plan + temporary dedicated capacity until model matching improves.
Tom (infra): Action items: 1) Tom + Raj: prototype reservation API and route decision service (due 2065432400). 2) Priya: finalize policy DSL and RFC (due 2065432200). 3) Aisha: write GA launch criteria + customer docs draft (due 2065432300). 4) Lena: draft contract language and list initial customers asking for residency (due 2065432350).
Aisha (prod): Thanks — will run a cross-functional kickoff after Priya posts RFC. Keep thread for quick updates. :thumbsup:
